job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let’s clarify some common doubts about chemical reactions. Rohan, you mentioned that balancing equations involves changing subscripts like H2O2. That is incorrect because changing subscripts alters the identity of the substance itself. Instead, we adjust the coefficients in front of formulas to ensure the number of atoms of each element remains equal on both sides, following the law of conservation of mass. Priya, you asked if rancidity is caused by bacteria. Actually, rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils in food, which happens even without bacteria, leading to unpleasant smells. Speaking of oxidation, it is not limited to reactions where oxygen is a reactant; it also includes the loss of electrons or the removal of hydrogen. Finally, let’s look at displacement. Some students think any metal can displace another, but a metal can only displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution. For example, zinc can displace copper, but copper cannot displace zinc. Remember, these rules help us predict chemical behavior accurately without guessing.

items.evidence: That is incorrect because changing subscripts alters the identity of the substance itself.
items.q: Why can't we balance an equation by changing a subscript in a formula?
options: It turns the substance into a different one
It breaks the law of conservation of mass
It changes the state of the substance
It adds extra molecules to one side only
items.explain: Changing a subscript changes which substance the formula stands for, so balancing must use coefficients.

wrong.why: mixes up the law with the reason for coefficients
confuses formula changes with state symbols
thinks balancing is about counting molecules

items.evidence: Actually, rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils in food, which happens even without bacteria, leading to unpleasant smells.
items.q: Chips kept in a sealed, germ-free bag still smell bad after months. What explains this?
options: Their oils slowly react with oxygen
Tiny germs inside are eating the oils
Heat from the bag keeps the reaction going
The chips lose electrons to the plastic
items.explain: Rancidity is oxidation of fats and oils, which can happen even without bacteria.

wrong.why: grabs the electron idea from the passage wrongly

items.evidence: Speaking of oxidation, it is not limited to reactions where oxygen is a reactant; it also includes the loss of electrons or the removal of hydrogen.
items.q: A substance loses hydrogen in a reaction with no oxygen present. What has happened to it?
items.explain: Oxidation also includes removal of hydrogen or loss of electrons, so oxygen is not always needed.

wrong.why: confuses oxidation with balancing an equation

items.evidence: For example, zinc can displace copper, but copper cannot displace zinc.
items.q: A copper rod is placed in zinc sulphate solution. What will most likely happen?
options: No reaction, as copper is less reactive
Copper displaces zinc from the solution
Zinc forms a precipitate on the rod
Copper and zinc swap places in turn
items.explain: Copper is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc from its salt solution.

wrong.why: thinks any metal can displace another
